Building a search engine has 3 big parts:

  • Crawling/indexing
  • Information retrieval
  • Curation

For crawling and indexing you will need to scan the internet for all address with port 80 open. Then you see if they have a sitemap or robots.txt to help you out, then download and parse their text or html content from the index out to all anchors, while ignoring circular references. Depending on the features you want for your search results, and then you will have to analyze that data for keywords and valuable information, you know, separate the wheat from the chaff.

Then you do a nslookup to see if there are any domain names that to to that up, and index the keywords and domain name if applicable in an information retrieval engine such as Lucene.

Now you build your interface and your api, and you do some natural language processing to extract keywords from user queries, and translate those into structured lucene queries, and pull the information and serialize it to be displayed to the user.

And then there's the curation part, you'll have to write something else to go over all of your indexes data and look for indicators that it's not what you want in your search engine, and then flag it, and then probably manually review for removal.

And on top of all that, you have to manage the infrastructure

What we really need is to decentralize this process, so that organizations with smaller budgets could create their own search engines. One possibility is to decentralize the crawling to some kind of a P2P algorithm. You can also have open data sharing between search engines (ex. dump ZIM files per domain), so every engine doesn't have to crawl every site.
